title: Sequential Valorization of Second-Grade Fig (Ficus carica L.) Biomass Through Hydroalcoholic Extraction and Jam Production for a Circular Bioeconomy
content: Second-grade figs can be valorized through sequential food-processing strategies that improve agricultural biomass utilization. This study evaluated hydroalcoholic extraction from Black Mission figs (Ficus carica L.) followed by jam production using the recovered residual biomass. Three independent batches, each containing 1 kg of sanitized fresh figs, underwent maceration for five days. The extract, residual biomass, and jam were characterized for physicochemical properties, total phenolic content (TPC), and DPPH antioxidant capacity. Each batch yielded 1435 ± 13 mL of extract, with an apparent volumetric recovery of 95.6 ± 0.4%, and 920 ± 7.5 g of residual biomass. The extract contained 21.50 ± 0.05% (v/v) alcohol, 62.33 ± 0.89 mg gallic acid equivalents (GAE)/L of TPC, and 423.81 ± 6.77 µmol Trolox equivalents (TE)/L of DPPH capacity. The residual biomass was converted into 1275 ± 8.2 g of jam per batch, with 65.18 ± 0.04 °Brix and pH 4.62 ± 0.02. The jam contained 181.74 ± 1.69 mg GAE/kg and showed a DPPH capacity of 327.67 ± 3.86 µmol TE/kg. These results demonstrate the technical feasibility of obtaining two food products sequentially from second-grade fig biomass and support its potential valorization within a circular bioeconomy.
